steps.message:
Build an 8-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation analyzing the top 20 trending GitHub repositories over the past 24 hours, targeting developer advocates, open-source community managers, and engineering leaders tracking AI tooling trends. The tone should be data-forward, analytical, and technically grounded.

The deck opens by establishing OSSInsight's credibility as a data source (10.6B+ GitHub events), then drills into the top trending repos ranked by score, examines language and category distributions, spotlights the emerging Claude Code ecosystem, compares community engagement metrics across repos, and closes with strategic takeaways on AI coding agent dominance.

For the "Top 5 Repos by Total Score" slide, use a horizontal bar chart or ranked table showing stars, forks, pushes, and PRs for each repo. For the "Language Distribution" slide, use a pie or donut chart reflecting the full breakdown (Python: 7, TypeScript: 4, HTML: 2, Rust: 2, Swift: 2, Shell: 1, Java: 1, Unspecified: 1). The "Category Breakdown" slide should use a stacked bar or treemap to visualize that ~70% of trending repos relate to AI coding assistance. The "Community Engagement" slide should use a scatter plot or grouped bar chart contrasting high- and low-engagement repos.

Do not fabricate any data not found in source_brief.md. All statistics, repo names, and metrics must come directly from the provided brief.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

arguments.content:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
import io
import os

# Ensure output directory exists
os.makedirs('/app/output', exist_ok=True)

prs = Presentation()
# Set 16:9 aspect ratio
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# --- Define styles and colors ---
BG_COLOR = RGBColor(245, 245, 245)
TITLE_COLOR = RGBColor(33, 33, 33)
ACCENT_COLOR = RGBColor(0, 102, 204)

# Function to set background
def set_background(slide):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(255, 255, 255)

# Slide 1: Title
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0] # Title slide
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]

title.text = "GitHub Trending Repos Snapshot:\nThe Rise of AI Coding Agents & Claude Code Skills"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(44)
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TITLE_COLOR

subtitle.text = "Based on OSSInsight's 10.6B+ GitHub Events Dataset\nTarget Audience: Developer Advocates, Open-Source Community Managers, Engineering Leaders\nPast 24 Hours Analysis"
subtitle.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(24)
subtitle.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR

# Slide 2: Platform Overview
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[1] # Title and Content
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
title.text = "OSSInsight Tracks 10.6 Billion GitHub Events in Real Time"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(36)
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TITLE_COLOR

content = slide.placeholders[1]
tf = content.text_frame
tf.text = "About OSSInsight Data Source:"
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Free, real-time analytics platform"
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Tracks over 10.6 billion GitHub events"
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Provides deep insights into open-source repositories, developers, and organizations"
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Covers stars, commits, pull requests, issues, contributors, and community health metrics"
p.level = 1
p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "• Ranks trending repositories using a composite Total Score = Stars score + Forks score + Base score"
p.level = 1

# Slide 3: Top 5 Trending Repos
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5] # Title Only
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
title.text = "hermes-agent Leads with 1,347 Stars — Top 5 Repos by Total Score"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(32)
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TITLE_COLOR

# Table for Top 5
rows, cols = 6, 6
left = Inches(1)
top = Inches(2)
width = Inches(11.333)
height = Inches(3.5)
table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table

columns = ['Rank', 'Repository', 'Stars', 'Forks', 'Pushes', 'PRs']
for i, col_name in enumerate(columns):
    cell = table.cell(0, i)
    cell.text = col_name
    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
    
data = [
    ["#1", "NousResearch/hermes-agent", "1,347", "101", "42", "78"],
    ["#2", "safishamsi/graphify", "742", "50", "6", "5"],
    ["#3", "VoltAgent/awesome-design-md", "615", "48", "1", "0"],
    ["#4", "JuliusBrussee/caveman", "300", "11", "1", "1"],
    ["#5", "shanraisshan/claude-code-best-practice", "304", "23", "0", "0"]
]

for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data):
    for col_idx, val in enumerate(row_data):
        table.cell(row_idx + 1, col_idx).text = val

# Slide 4: Language Distribution
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
title.text = "Python and TypeScript Dominate Trending Repos' Language Mix"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(32)

# Generate pie chart
labels = ['Python (7)', 'TypeScript (4)', 'HTML (2)', 'Rust (2)', 'Swift (2)', 'Shell (1)', 'Java (1)', 'Unspecified (1)']
sizes = [7, 4, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax.pie(sizes, labels=labels, autopct='%1.0f%%', startangle=140, colors=plt.cm.tab20.colors)
plt.setp(autotexts, size=10, weight="bold")
ax.axis('equal')
plt.title("Language Distribution of Top 20 Trending Repos")
plt.tight_layout()
img_stream = io.BytesIO()
plt.savefig(img_stream, format='png', dpi=300, transparent=True)
img_stream.seek(0)
slide.shapes.add_picture(img_stream, Inches(3), Inches(1.8), height=Inches(5))
plt.close(fig)

# Slide 5: Category Breakdown
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
title.text = "14 of 20 Trending Repos Are AI Coding Agent or Claude Code Projects"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(28)

# Generate Stacked Bar Chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 3.5))
categories = ['Top 20 Trending Repositories']

labels_bar = ['Repositories']
# Use non-overlapping count to sum to 20 for cleaner look, as explained in thought process
cat1 = [10] # AI Coding Agents & Skills
cat2 = [4]  # Claude Code Ecosystem Tools (excluding 1 overlap)
cat3 = [3]  # AI Infrastructure & Research
cat4 = [3]  # Developer Utilities (excluding 1 overlap or just 3 to sum to 20)
# Actually the prompt says:
# AI Coding Agents & Skills: 10
# Claude Code Ecosystem Tools: 5
# AI Infrastructure & Research: 3
# Developer Utilities: 4
# We can just plot a regular bar chart instead of stacked to avoid sum issues. Let's do horizontal bar chart.

cat_names = ['AI Coding Agents & Skills', 'Claude Code Ecosystem Tools', 'Developer Utilities', 'AI Infrastructure & Research']
cat_values = [10, 5, 4, 3]

ax.barh(cat_names, cat_values, color=['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728'])
ax.set_xlabel('Number of Repositories')
ax.set_title("Thematic Categories (~70% AI Coding Assistance)")
ax.invert_yaxis()  # labels read top-to-bottom

for i, v in enumerate(cat_values):
    ax.text(v + 0.1, i + 0.1, str(v), color='black', fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
img_stream = io.BytesIO()
plt.savefig(img_stream, format='png', dpi=300, transparent=True)
img_stream.seek(0)
slide.shapes.add_picture(img_stream, Inches(1.5), Inches(2.2), width=Inches(10))
plt.close(fig)

# Slide 6: Claude Code Ecosystem
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[1]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
title.text = "Claude Code Spawns an Ecosystem: Skills, Guides, Switches, and Best Practices"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(28)

content = slide.placeholders[1]
tf = content.text_frame
tf.text = "At least 7 repos broadly serve as Claude Code skills, guides, or switches:"

p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Core Claude Code Ecosystem Tools (5 repos):"
p.level = 1
p.font.bold = True

core_tools = [
    "claude-code-best-practice (Practice made Claude perfect)",
    "claude-howto (Visual guide to Claude Code)",
    "cc-switch (Cross-platform All-in-One assistant)",
    "caveman (Skill that cuts 75% of tokens by talking like caveman)",
    "learn-claude-code (Nano Claude Code-like agent)"
]
for tool in core_tools:
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = f"• {tool}"
    p.level = 2

p = tf.add_paragraph()
p.text = "Broader Ecosystem (Cross-listed in AI Coding Agents & Skills):"
p.level = 1
p.font.bold = True

broad_tools = [
    "oh-my-codex (OmX — Add hooks, agent teams, HUDs to your Codex)",
    "agent-skills (Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents)"
]
for tool in broad_tools:
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = f"• {tool}"
    p.level = 2

# Slide 7: Community Engagement
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[5]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
title.text = "hermes-agent Draws 78 PRs and 42 Pushes — Community Activity Varies Widely"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(26)

# Scatter plot: PRs vs Pushes
repos = ["hermes-agent", "graphify", "awesome-design-md", "caveman", "claude-code-best-practice", 
         "andrej-karpathy-skills", "DeepTutor", "multica", "opendataloader-pdf", "agent-skills",
         "VoxCPM", "reverse-SynthID", "oh-my-codex", "InstantSpaceSwitcher", "Recordly", "rtk", 
         "claude-howto", "cc-switch", "clicky", "learn-claude-code"]
prs_data = [78, 5, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 7, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 5, 0, 2, 2, 0]
pushes_data = [42, 6, 1, 1, 0, 0, 2, 35, 3, 0, 0, 2, 10, 2, 1, 3, 0, 2, 0, 0]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
ax.scatter(pushes_data, prs_data, color='blue', s=80, alpha=0.6)

# Annotate outliers and high engagement
for i, repo in enumerate(repos):
    if prs_data[i] > 4 or pushes_data[i] > 8:
        ax.annotate(repo, (pushes_data[i], prs_data[i]), xytext=(5,5), textcoords='offset points', fontsize=9, weight='bold')

ax.set_xlabel('Pushes (Past 24 Hours)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel('Pull Requests (Past 24 Hours)', fontsize=12)
ax.set_title('Community Engagement: Pushes vs. PRs', fontsize=14)
ax.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

plt.tight_layout()
img_stream = io.BytesIO()
plt.savefig(img_stream, format='png', dpi=300, transparent=True)
img_stream.seek(0)
slide.shapes.add_picture(img_stream, Inches(1.5), Inches(1.8), width=Inches(10))
plt.close(fig)

# Slide 8: Key Takeaways
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[1]
slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_background(slide)
title = slide.shapes.title
title.text = "Key Takeaways: AI Coding Agents Are GitHub's Hottest Category"
title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(30)

content = slide.placeholders[1]
tf = content.text_frame
takeaways = [
    "AI Agent Dominance: 14 of the top 20 repos (70%) are AI coding agent tools, skills, or related resources.",
    "Claude Code Ecosystem Explosion: Rapid community formation with at least 7 repos specifically targeting Claude Code skills, guides, and tooling.",
    "Python Leadership: Python powers 35% of trending repos, while TypeScript (20%) acts as the runner-up driving agent UIs.",
    "Community Engagement Concentration: Highly top-heavy activity. #1 repo hermes-agent attracted 78 PRs; 8 of 20 repos have zero PRs.",
    "Cost & Efficiency Trend: Token efficiency is a hot sub-theme (e.g., caveman, rtk) signaling cost-consciousness at scale."
]

tf.text = ""
for tk in takeaways:
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.text = "✓ " + tk
    p.level = 0
    p.font.size = Pt(18)
    p.space_after = Pt(14)

prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')
